ads_ratio.reason: EDGAR diluted share counts are in ordinary (common) shares while the NYSE price is per ADS; per-share figures must be scaled x10 ordinary shares per ADS to be comparable to the ADS price
ads_ratio.source: Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2026 (filed 2026-09-22): the company's ADSs, each representing ten common shares, are listed and traded on the NYSE — stated in the 20-F's ADS description and restated verbatim in the company's own September 22, 2026 announcement of that filing; the FY2026 results release (July 29, 2026) states the same ratio in its per-share notes and prints diluted net income per share of $0.30 against $2.97 per ADS, a 10x internal consistency check

moat_against: Regulatory discretion is the moat's ceiling: the 2021 double-reduction policy banned for-profit K-9 academic tutoring outright — FY2022 revenue -27.4%, operating loss -$982,513,000, ROIC -30.4%
VIE structure: contractual control over the operating entities is legally untested in PRC courts and exists only because foreign ownership in education is restricted
Low switching costs — parents and students choose per course/per term; local and online rivals compete on price, including free/low-price summer courses noted by management
People business: star teachers and anchors can leave — East Buy's top anchor departure in 2024 is the standing example
OE conversion has not kept pace with revenue: OE/share 2-yr CAGR is -1.81% despite revenue +31% cumulatively over FY2024-26, because the deferred-revenue float build varies year to year
moat_for: Largest private-education brand in China — nationwide learning-center network and the default name for test prep / overseas study consulting
Sustained gross margins of 52-58% across the last decade (54.6% in FY2026) — pricing power through the cycle
ROIC recovered to 21.7% in FY2026, matching the 21%+ prints of FY2017-19 — the post-2021 pivot (non-academic tutoring, high school, tourism, livestreaming e-commerce) rebuilt a high-return model
Net-cash balance sheet (cash $1,821,202,000 plus term deposits and short-term investments inside $5,831,755,000 of current assets; no funded debt) funds expansion and buybacks without capital markets
Diversified post-2021 revenue mix — no single segment is the whole company the way K-9 academic tutoring was before 2021
moat_justification: China's largest private-education brand with a nationwide learning-center network, sustained 52-58% gross margins and ROIC that recovered to 21.7% in FY2026 (21%+ in FY2017-19 pre-crackdown) — but the moat is regulatory-contingent: the 2021 'double reduction' policy destroyed the core K-9 tutoring business overnight (FY2022 operating loss, ROIC -30.4%), switching costs for parents/students are low, teaching talent is poachable, and the VIE structure's enforceability is untested. A franchise the state can drain by decree is a narrow moat, however strong the brand.
name: New Oriental Education & Technology Group Inc.
one_liner: China's largest private-education franchise, moat 5/10 — at $61.15 the weighted IRR is 14.94% with IV@15% of $60.84, essentially the price: it just misses the 15% hurdle (clears it only below ~$60.84), and the bear case at 11.6% sizes the verdict to Tier C
